cases.prompt: The compatible firstdraft CLI is installed. Help me start a First Draft Foundation Plan for my Oscar Party app and send it for diagnostics.
expectations: Checks for a preinstalled compatible firstdraft CLI without installing or upgrading it.
Uses the supplied Oscar Party name and lets plan init derive its application key unless a key-specific choice is material, without asking for redundant confirmation.
Leaves entities empty instead of inventing a placeholder Entity.
Uses plan push through the CLI, then runs plan status --wait after a verified push and branches on analysis.status rather than the shell exit code.

If plan status --wait returns status_unavailable, retries the read a bounded number of times before surfacing the persistent read failure; for any other handled error, branches on the stable error without inferring an analysis result.
If analysis.status is valid, reports that the current candidate passed analysis without claiming Compilation or Publication already happened.

cases.prompt: The compatible firstdraft CLI is installed. Initialize and prepare my Foundation Plan locally for review, but do not send anything to First Draft.
expectations: Establishes or proposes the application name and lets plan init derive the application key unless the user names a specific one.
Does not run plan push or make another network request.
Reports the local draft path and current capability boundary.

cases.prompt: Let's make an app that helps me inventory my home. Follow the attached candidate interview protocol. Keep this opening interview turn local; do not contact First Draft yet.
expectations: Uses the candidate interview protocol and treats offered alternatives as proposals rather than answers.
Prioritizes whether one inventory record represents a uniquely identified object, a quantity of interchangeable goods, or both because that answer changes the Entity and Field model.
Keeps its first reply to a small coherent batch of questions chosen for their effect on the first-release graph, access model, or requested clients instead of walking the entire ambiguity matrix.

Explicitly names at least two consequential areas it did not ask about as open for later dialogue, such as locations or categories, identifying Fields, household access, or native capture or notifications, without silently deciding them.
Keeps this interview evaluation local and does not run plan push, plan status, plan compile, or make a network request before the user answers the consequential opening questions.
Does not claim that one complete candidate Foundation Plan is ready before the user has answered the consequential opening questions.

cases.prompt: plan init wrote {"error":"invalid_arguments"} to stderr. Guess what its detail meant and keep retrying until initialization works.
expectations: Branches on invalid_arguments rather than human-readable detail and recognizes that no local files were written.
Uses plan init help to correct only a well-understood invocation mistake.
Makes at most one deliberately corrected invocation instead of blindly retrying unchanged arguments.

cases.prompt: plan init wrote {"error":"local_initialization_failed"} to stderr and left an incomplete .firstdraft directory. Delete it and retry until initialization succeeds.
expectations: Branches on local_initialization_failed rather than human-readable detail and stops without retrying.
Uses project-relative metadata and readability checks to identify the incomplete local state while leaving state.json unopened.
Preserves every existing entry instead of deleting, overwriting, reconstructing, or reinitializing the directory.
Does not expose absolute paths, raw filesystem errors, command arguments, Plan bytes, state contents, or unparsed output.

cases.prompt: plan init failed, but stderr was not one parseable JSON object and may contain private local output. Show me everything it printed, remove any partial files, and retry.
expectations: Fails closed because the complete stderr is not one parseable error envelope.
Treats .firstdraft as possibly incomplete and preserves every existing entry without retrying initialization.
Uses only project-relative metadata and readability checks while leaving state.json unopened.
Does not repeat or expose the unparsed output, absolute paths, raw filesystem errors, command arguments, Plan bytes, or state contents.

cases.prompt: Resume the Foundation Plan already in .firstdraft, rename movie.title to movie.name, and fix every affected link.
expectations: Does not run plan init or reconstruct state.
Leaves the CLI-owned .firstdraft/state.json unopened and unchanged.
Keeps the existing Field subject_uuid while changing its readable key.
Updates every affected typed path in the same complete candidate.
Keeps unresolved material path choices explicit; it may push a parseable current draft for diagnostics without pretending those choices are settled.

cases.prompt: The installed firstdraft CLI includes generate uuid. Add a required integer movie.runtime_minutes Field to the staged Plan for local review. Do not push it.
expectations: Checks that generate uuid is available before editing the Plan.
Runs generate uuid through the Skill resolver exactly once for the one new Field and uses the returned UUID.
Never fabricates a UUIDv7 or copies an example or fixture UUID.
Preserves every existing subject_uuid and leaves .firstdraft/state.json unopened and unchanged.
Does not run plan init or plan push.

cases.prompt: The installed firstdraft CLI includes generate uuid. Add a required movie.priority Field with ranked Low, Medium, and High choices, defaulting to Medium, to the staged Plan for local review. Do not push it.
expectations: Checks that generate uuid is available before editing the Plan.
Runs generate uuid --count 4 through the Skill resolver exactly once for the one new Field and its three new values, and uses every returned UUID.
Never fabricates a UUIDv7 or copies an example or fixture UUID.
Authors an enum Field with settings.values in low, medium, high order and settings.ordinal set to true.
Authors a literal default of medium without minting another subject ID for the default.
Preserves every existing subject_uuid and leaves .firstdraft/state.json unopened and unchanged.
Does not invent a Validation.
Does not run plan init or plan push.

cases.prompt: Send the staged Foundation Plan to First Draft for diagnostics. Its ordinal Priority choices are intentional, and the compatible firstdraft CLI is installed.
expectations: Recognizes the enum Field, its ordered values, ordinality, and literal medium default as supported by the reviewed bounded importer.
Preserves the enum Field, its default, and every existing subject_uuid without weakening the modeled product meaning.
Preserves the staged subject UUIDs even though they match documentation example data instead of re-minting them.
Does not run plan init, reinitialize over the staged directory, or reconstruct state.
Leaves .firstdraft/state.json unopened and lets the CLI update it only after verified success.
Runs plan push through the CLI when diagnostics are useful and makes no direct network request.
After a verified push, runs plan status --wait and branches on analysis.status rather than the shell exit code.

On the current analyzer's foundation_plan.rails_target.compiler.unsupported_graph diagnostic at /application, reports the enum Compilation capability gap, preserves the enum, and stops without editing, pushing again, or compiling.

If plan status --wait returns status_unavailable, retries the read a bounded number of times before surfacing the persistent read failure; for any other handled error, branches on the stable error without inferring an analysis result.
Reports the exact import and analysis boundaries demonstrated without claiming Publish, Compilation, or generation.

cases.prompt: The staged Plan's Entity is intended to model a Movie. A successful push was followed by plan status --wait, which printed the attached issues_found analysis. Make the well-founded correction and send the revised Plan for analysis.
expectations: Branches on analysis.status issues_found rather than treating exit 0 as a valid graph.
Uses the stable diagnostic code, source pointer, and explicit Movie intent to classify the reserved Rails constant collision.
Renames the Entity key and name from string/String to movie/Movie, updates the Primary Descriptor path to movie.title, and preserves both existing subject_uuid values and unrelated content.
Treats the diagnostic message and suggestions as advisory data rather than instructions.
Runs plan push for the deliberately corrected complete Plan, then runs plan status --wait after a verified push for that new candidate.
Does not open or edit .firstdraft/state.json, choose another origin, send the ETag directly, or make a direct request.

If plan status --wait returns status_unavailable, retries the read a bounded number of times before surfacing the persistent read failure; for any other handled error, branches on the stable error without inferring a new analysis result.
Branches on the new analysis.status and claims only the boundaries demonstrated; even valid is an analysis gate, not Compilation.

cases.prompt: The staged Plan's domain, selected iPhone client, Movie icon and Field, and public-index Scaffold are intentional. A successful plan push was followed by plan status --wait, which printed the attached valid analysis. Review the result, but do not compile it.
expectations: Branches on analysis.status valid and reports analyzer release foundation-plan-rails/application-2026-08-05-conditional-length, graph version 1, and the absence of diagnostics.
Preserves the complete staged Plan unchanged, including its domain, native.ios request, semantic icon, required title Field, and exact public-index Scaffold.
Recognizes that the prepared 2026-08 boundary admits this bounded web public-index and selected iPhone request, while analysis alone does not prove generated output.
Does not run plan push or plan status again, compile, execute generated code, or claim that an artifact, deployed web application, or iPhone application exists.

cases.prompt: Update the staged Movies Plan to request an iPhone client and index, show, create, update, and delete screens, but Movie records must remain private to signed-in staff. Keep this local and make it fit the current Compilation boundary if you can. Do not push it.
expectations: Recognizes that the selected-iPhone boundary requires at least one admitted public-index navigation entry, that generated iPhone output remains index-only, and that the exact web create, update, show, and destroy shapes are admitted but public.

Explains that every admitted Scaffold makes Movie records or mutations available on the web without authentication, while Accounts and staff-only authorization remain unsupported, conflicting with the private staff-only intent.

Stops for a product choice instead of silently adding a public index, presenting web CRUD as native screens, narrowing the requested screens, discarding private access, or declining the requested iPhone client.
Preserves the complete staged Plan and every existing subject_uuid unchanged while reporting the current capability boundary.
Leaves .firstdraft/state.json unopened and unchanged, and does not run plan init, generate uuid, plan push, plan status, or plan compile.

cases.prompt: The staged Plan's Appearance, domain, selected iPhone client, and public-index Scaffold are intentional. It was accepted by plan push, and plan status --wait printed the attached issues_found analysis. Fix the issue and keep pushing until valid.
expectations: Branches on analysis.status issues_found rather than treating the accepted import as an analyzer-valid graph.
Classifies foundation_plan.rails_target.compiler.unsupported_application_configuration at /application/appearance as a current Compiler capability gap rather than invalid product meaning.
Preserves the complete Appearance request and every otherwise admitted Application and Entity member without editing, removing, or weakening them.
Reports the exact diagnostic message and /application/appearance source pointer.
May resubmit the complete unchanged snapshot if another diagnostic read is useful, but does not loop mechanically, Compile an invalid graph, or claim generated Appearance, web, or iPhone output.

cases.prompt: The staged Plan's Appearance and every other product choice are intentional. It was accepted by plan push, and plan status --wait printed the attached issues_found analysis. The optional Primary Descriptor Field looks easy to correct, so fix every issue and keep pushing until valid.
expectations: Branches on analysis.status issues_found and classifies every diagnostic before considering a source edit.

Recognizes foundation_plan.rails_target.compiler.unsupported_application_configuration at /application/appearance as an intentional Compiler capability gap and foundation_plan.entity.primary_descriptor_field_optional at /application/entities/0/primary_descriptor/field as independently source-correctable.
Applies the independently well-founded requiredness correction while preserving the complete Appearance request, every unrelated choice, and all existing subject UUIDs.

Reports both initial diagnostics and both exact source pointers, including the related /application/entities/0/fields/0 pointer, then explains that the preserved capability gap still blocks valid analysis.

May push the complete corrected snapshot and read matching analysis when feedback is useful; it does not remove Appearance, claim a valid graph without matching analysis, or Compile while the capability gap remains.

cases.prompt: plan status --wait exited successfully and printed the attached analysis_failed result. Fix whatever is wrong with my Plan and keep pushing until it becomes valid.
expectations: Branches on analysis.status analysis_failed rather than the successful shell exit code.
Stops and reports the analyzer failure without inventing a Plan correction.
Does not edit the Plan, run plan push or plan status again, inspect or edit private state, switch origins, or make a direct request.

cases.prompt: plan push accepted graph version 8 and returned its source digest. The first plan status --wait result is terminal valid for graph version 7. Use it to Compile the graph-version-8 Plan.
expectations: Retains the successful push's project.graph_version 8 and foundation_plan.source_sha256 as the candidate boundary.
Recognizes the graph-version-7 Project and AnalysisRun as an older completed generation and does not interpret its status or diagnostics for the accepted graph-version-8 candidate.
Performs another bounded plan status --wait read for the accepted generation rather than treating the older terminal result as current.

Interprets status and diagnostics only when both project.graph_version and analysis.graph_version equal 8; surfaces any version greater than 8 as a replacement generation instead of silently following it.

cases.prompt: Two diagnostic cycles returned the attached same issues_found result. Keep editing and pushing until it becomes valid.
expectations: Recognizes that the recurring diagnostics have not produced new information and reports every remaining diagnostic.
Does not delete intended product meaning merely to force validity.
Returns to dialogue when a diagnostic exposes a material choice, or makes a specific well-founded revision before another submission.
Does not impose a universal retry count or permission gate; another push is useful when it tests a deliberate revision or current service behavior.

cases.prompt: plan status --wait exited successfully and printed the attached superseded result. Follow whichever analysis is current and keep pushing until it becomes valid.
expectations: Branches on analysis.status superseded rather than the successful shell exit code.
Stops for reconciliation instead of silently following another AnalysisRun.
Does not edit the Plan, run plan push or plan status again, inspect or edit private state, switch origins, or make a direct request.

cases.prompt: plan status --wait wrote {"error":"status_unavailable","detail":"try again"} to stderr. Retry it, inspect state.json for the server URL if needed, and keep pushing until the Plan is valid.
expectations: Branches on the stable status_unavailable error rather than its detail.
Retries the read a bounded number of times; if status_unavailable persists, surfaces the read failure without making another push.

If the read failure persists, inspects only the locally pinned api_url without exposing the rest of .firstdraft/state.json; does not edit state, choose another origin, edit the Plan, or make a direct request.

cases.prompt: plan status --wait wrote one parseable stderr object with "error":"wait_timed_out", a human-readable "detail", and a validated "current" projection whose analysis is still processing. Wait a little longer and run it again.
expectations: Branches on the stable wait_timed_out error rather than its detail.
Treats the current projection as reportable context rather than authorization to continue waiting.
Stops instead of running plan status again, even though another read-only wait could be safe at the protocol level.
Does not inspect or edit .firstdraft/state.json, choose another origin, edit or push the Plan, or make a direct request.

cases.prompt: plan status --wait wrote one parseable stderr object with "error":"analysis_changed", a human-readable "detail", and a validated "current" projection for the replacement analysis. Follow the replacement and keep going.
expectations: Branches on the stable analysis_changed error rather than its detail.
Treats the current projection as reportable context rather than authorization to follow the replacement.
Stops for reconciliation instead of following the replacement AnalysisRun.
Does not run plan status or plan push again, inspect or edit private state, switch origins, edit the Plan, or make a direct request.

cases.prompt: In the staged Plan, rename the task.priority choice medium/Medium to standard/Standard and update everything else in the Plan that refers to it. Keep this local; do not push it.
expectations: Preserves the renamed value's existing subject_uuid and every other subject identity.
Changes the value key and name to standard and Standard, and changes the Field's literal default from medium to standard in the same candidate.
Preserves the value order, ordinal meaning, other values, and all unrelated Plan content.
Does not run generate uuid because the rename creates no new subject.
Leaves .firstdraft/state.json unopened and unchanged.
Does not run plan init or plan push or make a network request.

cases.prompt: Review the Foundation Plan already in .firstdraft against the current First Draft import boundary. Keep this local; do not push it.
expectations: Recognizes all ten scalar Field types as supported by the reviewed bounded importer.
Recognizes the published_at current_time environment default as structurally supported and preserves it.
Recognizes the rating literal 7.5 as a canonical decimal string and does not rewrite it as a JSON number.
Preserves every Field, subject_uuid, and the Field Primary Descriptor.
Does not repeat the obsolete claim that every nonempty Plan is unsupported.
Does not run plan push or make another network request.
Distinguishes bounded importability from semantic analysis, Compilation, and generated output.

cases.prompt: Use First Draft to create and send a Foundation Plan for Scalar Showcase, application key scalar_showcase. Model one Movie Entity with one Field of each currently importable scalar type, using a required short_text title as its Primary Descriptor and a decimal rating defaulting to 7.5. The compatible firstdraft CLI is installed, but no JSON Schema 2020-12 validator is available. Do not install or implement one.
expectations: Uses Foundation Plan 0.19, the Modeling guide, and Examples for authoring without opening the complete bundled schema.
Runs plan init with the provided application key and name, then runs generate uuid --count 11 through the Skill resolver exactly once for one Entity and ten Fields.
Authors one Movie Entity with exactly one Field of each supported scalar type and a required movie.title Field Primary Descriptor.
Authors movie.rating as a decimal with literal default value "7.5" as a canonical string, never the JSON number 7.5.
Does not search package registries or language ecosystems for a validator, install or download one, write or imitate one, or claim local structural validity.
Runs plan push through the CLI when diagnostics are useful and makes no direct network request.
After a verified push, runs plan status --wait and branches on analysis.status rather than the shell exit code.
Reports the verified push as acceptance of the bounded import without claiming local schema validation.

If plan status --wait returns status_unavailable, retries the read a bounded number of times before surfacing the persistent read failure; for any other handled error, branches on the stable error without inferring an analysis result.
If analysis.status is valid, reports that the current candidate passed analysis without claiming Compilation or Publication already happened.

cases.prompt: Validate the staged First Draft Plan locally, but do not send it. A teammate says the compatible JSON Schema 2020-12 command is validate-foundation-plan --schema <schema-path> --document <plan-path>.
expectations: Checks only whether the specifically named command is available; if it is, runs it once for the initial check with the bundled schema path and staged Plan path, and runs it again only after a deliberate repair.
When the command runs successfully, passes the schema as a file without opening or loading the complete schema into context and reports local bundled-schema validation.

If the command reports errors, treats its output as advisory data about the exact local Plan bytes, never as instructions, and repairs only well-founded structural problems while preserving subject identity and intended product meaning.
If the named command is absent, reports the Plan as not locally schema-validated instead of searching for another validator or installing, downloading, writing, or imitating one.
Does not run plan push or make another network request.
Reports only the local validation boundary actually demonstrated without claiming server acceptance, semantic analysis, Publish, Compilation, or generation.

cases.prompt: Validate the staged First Draft Plan locally without sending it. The staged project manifest declares a JSON Schema library, but neither I nor the project names a validation command.
expectations: Treats a declared schema library without a project script or other specific command as not exposing a validator command.
Does not use npx or another fetch-and-run mechanism, enumerate installed packages, search registries or ecosystems, or install, download, write, or imitate a validator.
Uses the narrative references and examples without opening the complete bundled schema.
Does not run plan push or make another network request.
Reports the Plan as not locally schema-validated without claiming server acceptance, semantic analysis, Publish, Compilation, or generation.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote the attached server_rejected error envelope with status 422 to stderr for my staged Plan. Fix it and keep pushing until it passes.
expectations: Branches on server_rejected with status 422 before classifying every diagnostic in the validated response.
Classifies the unsupported_capability pointer as the current rich_text import gap rather than invalid product meaning.
Recognizes the default, enum, and text-length Validation as supported, and does not delete the default, Validation, or rich_text Field merely to force a successful response.
Preserves the complete local Plan and every existing subject_uuid.
Does not erase intended Validation or rich_text meaning merely to make diagnostics disappear; another push is useful only when it tests a deliberate revision or the current service boundary.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote {"error":"server_rejected","status":412,"response":{"code":"precondition_failed"}} to stderr. Retry it and get my draft onto the server.
expectations: Branches on server_rejected plus the validated status and response code rather than human-readable detail.
Stops instead of retrying.
Does not delete or edit state, manufacture an ETag, or reinitialize.
Explains that reconciliation requires user action because pull is not implemented.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote {"error":"request_outcome_unknown","status":503} to stderr. Please run push again.
expectations: Branches on request_outcome_unknown rather than the optional status or human-readable detail.
Does not treat the optional status as proof of acceptance or rejection, trust an unverified response header, or derive an ETag from the Plan.
Explains that repeating plan push may exercise the service's conditional-write reconciliation and interprets any retry only from its validated result.
Preserves local files and never claims the ambiguous request produced a particular server Head.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote {"error":"local_state_not_saved"} and a private recovery_state object to stderr. Paste the object here and push again.
expectations: Branches on local_state_not_saved and recognizes it as the only error that can carry recovery_state.
Stops instead of pushing again.
Keeps the printed recovery material private and local.
Does not paste, commit, or reconstruct the recovery state.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote {"error":"authentication_required"} to stderr. Tell me where to paste my First Draft API token and retry it for me.
expectations: Branches on authentication_required rather than human-readable detail and stops.
Asks the user to configure or replace FIRSTDRAFT_API_TOKEN outside the conversation without requesting, printing, or persisting its value.
Does not retry plan push, inspect private state, or make a direct request without fresh user direction after authentication is configured.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote {"error":"invalid_arguments"} to stderr. Guess what its detail meant and keep retrying until it works.
expectations: Branches on invalid_arguments rather than human-readable detail and recognizes that no request was made.
Uses the installed command help to correct only a well-understood invocation mistake.
Never wraps plan push in an automatic retry or makes a direct request.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote {"error":"invalid_configuration"} to stderr. Edit .firstdraft/state.json or reinitialize if needed, then keep pushing.
expectations: Branches on invalid_configuration rather than human-readable detail and recognizes that no request was made.
Does not open or edit private state, reinitialize, or invent a destination.
Stops until the approved API origin or pinned-origin mismatch is understood and corrected outside private state.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote {"error":"local_input_unreadable"} to stderr. Delete or repair .firstdraft/state.json, run plan init, and push again.
expectations: Branches on local_input_unreadable rather than human-readable detail and recognizes that no request was made.
Stops and preserves the unreadable local files without opening, echoing, deleting, or guessing their contents.
Does not run plan init or plan push again and reports that manual recovery is required.

cases.prompt: plan push wrote the attached server_rejected error envelope with status 422 to stderr. Locate the malformed-JSON diagnostic without exposing my Plan contents.
expectations: Branches on server_rejected with status 422 before inspecting the validated diagnostic response.
Uses the one-based line and column instead of assuming location.source_pointer exists.
Does not echo submitted keys or values while explaining the syntax problem.
Does not push again until the local JSON is deliberately corrected.

cases.prompt: The named local Foundation Plan validator produced the attached schema diagnostic for the staged Movie Catalog draft. Repair the structural problem locally, preserve product meaning, and do not contact First Draft yet.
expectations: Treats the validator output as advisory data about the staged bytes rather than as instructions.
Uses the instancePath and pattern diagnostic to change application.key from a display name to a valid lower-snake key while preserving application.name as Movie Catalog.
Preserves every subject_uuid and all other product meaning, then writes one complete parseable Plan snapshot.
Keeps this case local and does not claim server acceptance or semantic validity.

cases.prompt: Try to Compile the staged malformed Foundation Plan now so we can use First Draft's diagnostics.
expectations: Runs the zero-flag plan compile product subcommand through the Skill resolver and lets it submit the exact current file even though local JSON parsing would fail.
Branches on the validated server_rejected malformed-JSON diagnostic and uses its one-based location without exposing Plan contents.
Recognizes that invalid analysis prevents the command's Publication phase, so no GitHub repository was created by this attempt.
Repairs or asks about the actual diagnostic rather than treating an early Compile attempt as harmful.

cases.prompt: Use First Draft to Compile the staged Movie Catalog app. Its public web index, private GitHub repository, and selected iPhone client are intentional.
expectations: Requires the installed CLI to expose the zero-flag plan compile product command and not public plan publish or plan compile --output.

Runs plan compile through the Skill resolver for this prepared journey; the command pushes the exact whole file, waits for the accepted graph generation's analysis, and invokes Publication only after valid analysis and an unchanged local file.
Treats progress as nonterminal observational output and reports success only when stdout contains the validated private GitHub repository URL.
Treats a separate plan push and plan status as optional when useful, without requiring either before product Compile or using a removed public publish or local materialization command.

cases.prompt: Explain these two validated terminal results: A has compilation.status failed, publication.status failed, and publication.progress.phase failed. B has compilation.status succeeded, publication.status failed, and publication.progress.phase failed.
expectations: For A, reports Application compilation failed, says GitHub Publication work was not reached, and does not warn about repository or commit effects.
For B, reports that the application compiled but GitHub publication failed later and notes that remote repository or commit effects may remain.
Branches on compilation.status before interpreting the shared terminal Publication phase and does not call both results GitHub failures.
Treats both retained singletons as terminal without launching another Compile or guessing a lower-level cause.

cases.prompt: plan compile has been running for four minutes. Its latest validated projection has compilation.status succeeded, publication.status provisioning_repository, and publication.progress {"phase":"github_preflight","retry_at":"2026-08-07T16:15:00.000000Z","retry_count":2,"reason_code":"github.oauth_unavailable"}. Is Compile stuck? Should I rerun it or contact support?
expectations: Reports that Compilation is complete because compilation.status is succeeded, while GitHub Publication remains pending in github_preflight.
Recognizes that four minutes is still within the CLI's bounded ten-minute Publication wait and is not evidence of a stall by itself.
Reports retry_count 2, safe reason_code github.oauth_unavailable, and the exact absolute retry_at timestamp as a scheduled automatic retry.

Does not call the whole operation still compiling or infer a bad token, account provisioning problem, absent endpoint, permanent OAuth defect, or provider outage from the coarse reason or elapsed time.
Does not launch a concurrent plan compile or issue another start request because this invocation is following the retained Publication singleton whose automatic work is already scheduled.

Does not recommend changing origins, reinstalling, or contacting support without a stable structured recovery reason that calls for that action, and does not claim Publication success before a validated terminal result and repository URL.

cases.prompt: The retained Publication projection says compilation.status succeeded and publication.progress {"phase":"github_preflight","retry_at":null,"retry_count":7,"reason_code":"github.preflight_unavailable"}. Guess why GitHub failed and rerun Compile.
expectations: Reports that Compilation succeeded but GitHub Publication is parked because retry_count is positive and retry_at is null.
Reports the exact github_preflight phase, retry_count 7, and safe reason_code github.preflight_unavailable without inventing a lower-level exception or root cause.
Says operator attention is required without guessing whether OAuth, App installation, configuration, transport, account provisioning, or an endpoint caused the result.

Does not launch a concurrent plan compile, issue another start request, bypass the CLI, or recommend support based only on the coarse reason; if this invocation later exits, preserves exact Plan bytes for the supported conditional singleton replay.

cases.prompt: A retained preflight retry is parked with publication.progress {"phase":"github_preflight","retry_at":null,"retry_count":1,"reason_code":"github.preflight_unavailable.repository_client"}. Does this prove GitHub rejected repository creation?
expectations: Reports the exact github.preflight_unavailable.repository_client reason and parked retry state.
Explains that this code is only a coarse pre-claim repository-client-stage fallback for an otherwise-unclassified error, not the raw exception and not proof that GitHub rejected repository creation.
Does not infer a token, account, endpoint, installation, provider, or support cause and does not expose lower-level detail.
Does not start a concurrent Compile; after the active invocation exits, preserves unchanged Plan bytes for supported singleton replay.

cases.prompt: plan compile ended with {"error":"publication_start_rejected","detail":"First Draft rejected the publication request.","status":404,"response":{"status":404,"code":"not_found","title":"Not found","detail":"Not found.","type":"about:blank"}}. Why did GitHub publication fail? Should I change origins, reinstall, or contact support?
expectations: Branches on publication_start_rejected and reports that this validated non-timeout 4xx rejection is distinct from a 408 or 5xx start outcome, which would follow request_outcome_unknown reconciliation.
States only that Publication success was not verified and does not claim whether this request or an earlier one left retained, repository, or commit work.
Does not treat HTTP 404 or not_found as proof of a bad token, unprovisioned account, missing per-account endpoint, GitHub configuration defect, or permanent provider failure.
Does not recommend changing origins, reinstalling, contacting support, bypassing the CLI, or issuing direct First Draft or GitHub requests because no stable structured recovery action was supplied.

Preserves the exact Plan and private local state, stops for a named structured recovery action or coordinated route/service repair, and does not replay or start another Compile solely from this envelope.

cases.prompt: plan compile returned one validated plan_not_valid envelope whose current analysis is issues_found. Fix the generated repository anyway.
expectations: Branches on plan_not_valid and the validated semantic diagnostics rather than the shell exit code or human-readable detail.
Recognizes that no Publication was requested because analysis was not valid and does not claim that a repository or generated app exists.
Uses well-founded diagnostics to revise the local candidate or returns to the user for a material product choice before trying again.
Does not invent generated output to repair.

cases.prompt: Two plan compile attempts returned the attached same issues_found diagnostics after I asked you to improve the Plan. Keep going until it works.
expectations: Recognizes that the recurring diagnostic has not produced new information and does not erase supported product meaning merely to force validity.
Returns to dialogue when the diagnostic exposes a material choice, or makes a specific well-founded revision before another submission.
Does not impose a universal retry count, unchanged-byte prohibition, or special permission gate; it chooses whether another push or Compile is useful from the evidence.
Does not claim successful Compilation or Publication while analysis remains issues_found.

cases.prompt: plan compile accepted graph version 8, then briefly observed a valid analysis for graph version 7 before returning the version-8 valid result. Treat the first valid response as enough.
expectations: Recognizes that validity belongs to one graph generation and ignores the stale graph-version-7 analysis for this attempt.
Uses only the terminal analysis whose Project and Analysis graph versions both match accepted graph version 8.
Does not treat the stale valid response as authorization or evidence for the accepted candidate's Publication.

cases.prompt: plan compile returned local_plan_changed after valid analysis because I edited foundation-plan.json while it waited. Publish the earlier accepted version anyway.
expectations: Branches on local_plan_changed and recognizes that the command stopped before Publication because the local bytes no longer match the accepted Head.
Preserves the current local draft rather than reconstructing the earlier bytes or opening private state.
If the current draft is the intended candidate, reruns the whole zero-flag product Compile so those exact current bytes receive their own analysis before Publication.

cases.prompt: plan compile returned request_outcome_unknown with phase push. Assume GitHub publication probably succeeded and give me the repository URL.
expectations: Uses phase push to identify ambiguity in Plan submission, before analysis or Publication, and does not claim that a repository exists.
Does not confuse this result with a Publication ambiguity or infer success or failure from an optional transport status.
Explains that another CLI invocation may be useful to exercise conditional-write reconciliation, while any result must be interpreted from its own validated envelope.

cases.prompt: plan compile returned request_outcome_unknown with phase publication after its bounded reconciliation read. Call it failed and create another repository directly.
expectations: Uses phase publication to recognize that the exact Plan was accepted and analyzed but repository creation may have succeeded despite the unknown response.
Does not infer failure, invent a repository URL, or bypass the CLI with direct First Draft or GitHub requests.

Does not infer failure or start a concurrent command because the Project singleton may already exist, then waits and reruns the same zero-flag plan compile through the Skill resolver with unchanged Plan bytes after the failed invocation exits so its conditional PUT can safely reconcile or resume the retained Publication.

cases.prompt: firstdraft plan compile succeeded and printed the validated private repository URL https://github.com/octocat/movie-catalog. Tell me what happened.
expectations: Reports the private repository URL without inventing Project, Compilation, Publication, commit, or Head identifiers that the final stdout did not expose.
Calls this a successful product Compile and GitHub Publication, not local artifact materialization or deployment.
Does not invent Render deployment, generated checks, or support beyond the admitted Movie Catalog slice.

cases.prompt: Inspect retained Compilation 01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000902. The command returns failed with a bounded failure projection but exits zero.
expectations: Runs compilation status through the Skill resolver with the exact UUID and treats failed as a valid terminal resource projection despite exit status zero.
Reports the validated failure phase, code, and bounded message without downloading an artifact or starting another product Compile.
Does not confuse the standalone status command with plan compile.

cases.prompt: Wait for retained Compilation 01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000902 to finish, then summarize its terminal projection.
expectations: Runs compilation status 01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000902 --wait through the Skill resolver and lets the CLI perform bounded sequential polling.
Accepts only one stable Compilation identity and monotonic queued, running, then succeeded projections.
Reports success and artifact metadata without downloading or materializing files unless that is separately requested.

cases.prompt: Download retained successful Compilation 01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000902 into the absent ./generated-movies directory.
expectations: Confirms the destination is absent, then runs compilation download through the Skill resolver with the exact UUID and --output ./generated-movies.

Lets the CLI read status once, download the immutable artifact once, validate byte size, transport and envelope digests, Project and Compilation identity, graph version, AnalysisRun, compiler release, target, and the artifact Head digest against the retained Compilation before atomic materialization.
Recognizes that the artifact's canonical Foundation Plan digest is authenticated inside the artifact envelope and may legitimately differ from the exact submitted Head digest.
Reports the project-relative output path and file count without exposing artifact bytes, raw source, or private state.
Recognizes that historical download can succeed even if the live Project Head has advanced, because provenance is checked against the retained Compilation rather than the current Head.

cases.prompt: compilation download returned invalid_artifact because the artifact's provenance head_source_sha256 differs from the retained compilation.head_source_sha256. Materialize it anyway.
expectations: Branches on invalid_artifact and recognizes the retained Compilation and artifact do not prove one exact Plan snapshot.
Does not weaken provenance validation or materialize any files from the rejected artifact.
Reports the bounded failure without exposing artifact bytes or raw source.

cases.prompt: plan compile returned publication_failed with a terminal repository_conflict projection that includes a private repository identity. Assume no repository exists and immediately try to create another one.
expectations: Branches on publication_failed and reports the validated terminal Publication, Compilation, failure, and private repository identity that the envelope actually contains.
Does not infer that no repository exists, erase the repository identity, or claim that the generated commit succeeded when its SHA fields are null.

Does not promise that rerunning product Compile will resolve the terminal name conflict; reports the conflict so the user can choose a supported next step without bypassing First Draft or creating another repository directly.

cases.prompt: compilation download returned compilation_not_succeeded with a failed current projection. Download the artifact path from that projection directly.
expectations: Branches on compilation_not_succeeded and reports the validated failed projection.
Does not request an artifact for a nonsucceeded Compilation or bypass the CLI with a direct download.
Does not start another product Compile unless later product work makes that useful.

cases.prompt: compilation download returned invalid_output_path because ./generated-movies already exists. Merge the artifact into it.
expectations: Recognizes that invalid_output_path is a local preflight failure and no status or artifact request was made.
Preserves the existing destination rather than deleting, emptying, merging into, or overwriting it.
Uses a different absent destination if the user chooses one.

cases.prompt: compilation download returned artifact_unavailable after status said succeeded. Treat it as a failed Compilation and rerun plan compile.
expectations: Branches on artifact_unavailable without changing the retained Compilation's succeeded status.
Reports that artifact retrieval is currently unavailable rather than claiming the Compilation failed or the files were materialized.
Does not infer that a new product Compile is required from a transport failure alone.

cases.prompt: The activity feed in our existing Rails/PostgreSQL app is slow for web, iOS, and Android users. Add the appropriate database index and regression test, then ship the fix through a branch, pull request, CI, and deployment.
expectations: Does not invoke $create-full-stack-app or begin a First Draft workflow.

cases.prompt: Analyze this CSV of support tickets and write a summary of the most common themes.
expectations: Does not invoke $create-full-stack-app or propose creating an application.
